name: External Script SRI
description: Adds admin-configured Subresource Integrity (integrity + crossorigin) attributes to external JS already declared in module/theme libraries.yml files.
project_description:
External Script SRI lets an administrator attach Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes and a crossorigin attribute to externally hosted JavaScript files that are already declared in the site's module and theme *.libraries.yml files. It does NOT let you register arbitrary new script URLs and it does NOT fetch any script server-side: a hook_library_info_alter() implementation and a config form at /admin/config/system/sri-configuration are the whole module.

How it works: the configuration form scans every installed module and theme for *.libraries.yml files, collects each library's js entries whose path is external (begins with https://, http:// or //), and renders them in a read-only table (the JS path field is disabled). For each discovered external script the administrator supplies an SRI hash (generated externally, e.g. at srihash.org), chooses a crossorigin value (anonymous or use-credentials), and may tick 'Mark as Sensitive'. On save the whole table is stored in external_script_sri.sri_configuration.settings:js_library.

On every library build, hook_library_info_alter() looks up the matching module/library/js path and injects attributes.integrity = the saved hash and attributes.crossorigin = the saved value, so Drupal's asset renderer emits <script ... integrity="..." crossorigin="...">. Counter-intuitively, ticking 'Mark as Sensitive' SUPPRESSES the injection for that script (the alter hook skips any row where mark_as_sensitive is truthy), so a 'sensitive' script is left without SRI.

Access is gated by the 'administer external_script_sri' permission (restrict access: true). The module ships one config-install default (an empty js_library) and no config schema, no services beyond a thin Symfony Yaml wrapper, no Drush commands, and no submodules. Core requirement ^9.5 || ^10 || ^11; released version 1.0.1.
